chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Is-haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in using the monetary valuation (qimah) for the Fitrah (alms of fasting)."

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr, the alms given at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay the monetary value instead of food for Zakat al-Fitr?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits paying the value (qimah) of Zakat al-Fitr in money, reflecting the juristic flexibility to adapt the obligation to contemporary economic conditions. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for allowing monetary payment, which facilitates the distribution of aid to the poor in modern contexts where food distribution may be less practical.
